poem_in_farsi:
من ظاهرِ نیستی و هستی دانم،
من باطنِ هر فراز و پستی دانم؛
با این‌همه از دانشِ خود شَرْمَم باد،
گر مرتبه‌ای وَرایِ مستی دانم
poem_in_english:
Man zāher-e nisti o hasti dānam,
Man bāten-e har farāz o pasti dānam;
Bā in hame az dānesh-e khod sharmam bād,
Gar martabeh-ee varāye masti dānam.
poem_in_english_translation:
I know the outer face of void and being,
I know the inner truth of rise and fall;
Yet for all my knowing, let me be ashamed,
If I know any rank beyond being drunk.
meaning:
1. I understand the basic concept of existence and non-existence.
2. I grasp the deeper meaning of life's ups and downs.
3. Despite all my knowledge, I am humbled and ashamed by it.
4. If I think there is a higher truth beyond drunkenness.
implications_for_21st_century: The poem implies that despite our vast knowledge, true wisdom may lie in embracing the present moment.
poetic_traslation:
I know the seen and unseen, existence I embrace,
I comprehend the inner depths and the surface's grace;
Yet, my knowledge brings shame and a modest quest,
Yearning for insights beyond, an intoxicated space.
title_in_farsi: من ظاهرِ نیستی و هستی دانم
title_in_english: I know the outer face of void and being

poem_in_farsi:
آن قصر که بر چرخ همی‌زد پهلو،
بر درگه آن شاه همی‌دید زانو؛
دیدیم که بر کنگره‌اش فاخته‌ای
بنشسته همی‌گفت: که کو کو، که کو کو؟
poem_in_english:
Ān qasr ke bar charkh hami-zad pahlū,
Bar dargah-e ān shāh hami-did zānū;
Didim ke bar kangore-ash fākhte-i
Benshaste hami-goft: ke kū kū, ke kū kū?
poem_in_english_translation:
That palace that rivaled the sky in grandeur,
Where kings would kneel at its great door;
We saw a turtledove perched on its battlement,
Cooing: where are they? where are they?
meaning: The grandest palaces and most powerful kings eventually fade. Nature reclaims what humans build.
implications_for_21st_century: Even the mightiest achievements are temporary. Focus on what truly matters rather than accumulating power or wealth.
poetic_traslation:
That palace whose pillars once brushed the sky,
Where kings once knelt as ages drifted by;
A turtledove now perches on its wall,
And coos: where are they now? where are they? why?
title_in_farsi: آن قصر که بر چرخ همی‌زد پهلو
title_in_english: That palace that rivaled the sky

poem_in_farsi:
ابر آمد و باز بر سرِ سبزه گریست،
بی بادهٔ گلرنگ نمی‌باید زیست؛
این سبزه که امروز تماشاگهِ ماست،
فردا همه از خاکِ ما برخواهد رُست.
poem_in_english:
Abr āmad o bāz bar sar-e sabze gerist,
Bi bāde-ye golrang nami-bāyad zist;
In sabze ke emruz tamāshāgah-e māst,
Fardā hame az khāk-e mā bar-khāhad rust.
poem_in_english_translation:
The cloud came and wept again upon the green,
Without rose-colored wine one must not live;
This grass that is our spectacle today,
Tomorrow from our dust it all shall grow.
meaning: Rain nurtures the earth, and life is fleeting. We should enjoy the present because we will become part of the earth.
implications_for_21st_century: Life is cyclical. Enjoy the present moment because we are all part of nature's cycle of renewal.
poetic_traslation:
The clouds have wept upon the meadow green,
Without the rosy wine, life should not be seen;
This grass we gaze upon with joy today,
Tomorrow from our dust shall rise serene.
title_in_farsi: ابر آمد و باز بر سرِ سبزه گریست
title_in_english: The cloud came and wept upon the green

poem_in_farsi:
بر چهرهٔ گل نسیمِ نوروز خوش است،
در صحنِ چمن روی دل‌افروز خوش است؛
از دی که گذشت هر چه گویی خوش نیست،
خوش باش و ز دی مگو که امروز خوش است.
poem_in_english:
Bar chehre-ye gol nasim-e nowruz khosh ast,
Dar sahn-e chaman rūy-e del-afrūz khosh ast;
Az dey ke gozasht har che gūyi khosh nist,
Khosh bāsh o ze dey magū ke emrūz khosh ast.
poem_in_english_translation:
The Nowruz breeze on the face of the rose is sweet,
In the garden's court a radiant face is sweet;
Of yesterday that passed, whatever you say is not sweet,
Be happy and speak not of yesterday — today is sweet.
meaning: Do not dwell on the past. The present moment — like Nowruz and spring — is what is beautiful and worth celebrating.
implications_for_21st_century: Stop dwelling on the past. Embrace today.
poetic_traslation:
Upon the rose the breath of spring is sweet,
Within the garden, beauty's glow is sweet;
Of yesterday, whatever you may say, is bitter—
Be glad! Speak not of yesterday — today is sweet.
title_in_farsi: بر چهرهٔ گل نسیمِ نوروز خوش است
title_in_english: The Nowruz breeze on the rose is sweet

poem_in_farsi:
این کوزه چو من عاشقِ زاری بوده‌ست،
در بندِ سرِ زلفِ نگاری بوده‌ست؛
این دسته که بر گردنِ او می‌بینی،
دستی‌ست که بر گردنِ یاری بوده‌ست.
poem_in_english:
In kūze cho man āsheq-e zāri būdast,
Dar band-e sar-e zolf-e negāri būdast;
In daste ke bar gardan-e ū mi-bini,
Dasti-st ke bar gardan-e yāri būdast.
poem_in_english_translation:
This jug, like me, was once a wretched lover,
Entangled in a beauty's curling hair;
This handle that you see upon its neck,
Was once a hand upon a lover's neck.
meaning: Everything around us once had life and love. Objects carry the memory of past lives.
implications_for_21st_century: We are all connected through time. The matter that makes up our world has lived and loved before.
poetic_traslation:
This jug was once a lover, lost in sighs,
Ensnared by flowing locks and shining eyes;
This handle clinging to its neck you see,
Was once an arm in love's sweet enterprise.
title_in_farsi: این کوزه چو من عاشقِ زاری بوده‌ست
title_in_english: This jug was once a wretched lover

poem_in_farsi:
چون عمر به سر رسد چه بغداد و چه بلخ،
پیمانه چو پر شود چه شیرین و چه تلخ؛
می نوش که بعد از من و تو ماه بسی
از سلخ به غره آید از غره به سلخ.
poem_in_english:
Chon omr be sar rasad che Baghdād o che Balkh,
Peymāne cho por shavad che shirin o che talkh;
Mey nūsh ke ba'd az man o to māh basi
Az salkh be ghorre āyad az ghorre be salkh.
poem_in_english_translation:
When life is done, what matter Baghdad or Balkh?
When the cup is full, what matter sweet or bitter?
Drink wine! For after you and me, many a moon
Shall wane to new, and wax from new to wane.
meaning: When life ends, worldly distinctions don't matter. Time will continue its cycle long after we're gone.
implications_for_21st_century: Our differences and achievements are meaningless in the face of death. Time is indifferent to us.
poetic_traslation:
When life is spent, what's Baghdad or what's Balkh?
When brimming full, what's sweetness, what is gall?
Drink deep! For after you and me the moon
Shall wane and wax through many a rise and fall.
title_in_farsi: چون عمر به سر رسد چه بغداد و چه بلخ
title_in_english: When life is done what matter Baghdad or Balkh

poem_in_farsi:
می خور که به زیرِ گِل بسی خواهی خفت،
بی‌مونس و بی‌رفیق و بی‌همدم و جفت؛
زنهار! به کس مگو تو این رازِ نهفت:
هر لاله که پژمرد نخواهد بشکفت.
poem_in_english:
Mey khor ke be zir-e gel basi khāhi khoft,
Bi-mūnes o bi-rafiq o bi-hamdam o joft;
Zenhār! Be kas magū to in rāz-e nahoft:
Har lāle ke pazhmord nakhāhad beshkoft.
poem_in_english_translation:
Drink wine, for long beneath the clay you'll sleep,
Without companion, friend, or mate, or pair;
Beware! Tell no one this hidden truth:
Every tulip that has wilted shall not bloom again.
meaning: Death is final and lonely. Enjoy life while you can, for there is no return.
implications_for_21st_century: Face mortality honestly. Life is finite — once gone, it does not return.
poetic_traslation:
Drink deep, for long beneath the earth you'll sleep,
Without a friend or lover there to keep;
Beware! This secret tell to none alive:
Each wilted tulip shall no more its petals reap.
title_in_farsi: می خور که به زیرِ گِل بسی خواهی خفت
title_in_english: Drink wine for long beneath the clay you'll sleep

poem_in_farsi:
ای دوست بیا تا غمِ فردا نخوریم،
وین یکدمِ عمر را غنیمت شمریم؛
فردا که ازین دیرِ کهن در گذریم،
با هفت‌هزارسالگان سر به سریم.
poem_in_english:
Ey dūst biā tā gham-e fardā nakhūrim,
V-in yek dam-e omr rā ghanimat shemarim;
Fardā ke az-in deyr-e kohan dar gozarim,
Bā haft-hazār-sālegān sar be sarim.
poem_in_english_translation:
O friend, come, let us not grieve for tomorrow,
And count this one breath of life as a treasure;
Tomorrow when we depart this ancient inn,
We shall be level with those seven thousand years gone.
meaning: Do not worry about the future. Cherish each moment, for we will all join those who came before us.
implications_for_21st_century: Live in the present. Anxiety about the future is wasted energy.
poetic_traslation:
O friend, come let us not for tomorrow grieve,
This fleeting breath of life as treasure cleave;
Tomorrow when we leave this ancient inn,
With those of seven thousand years we'll be as leaves.
title_in_farsi: ای دوست بیا تا غمِ فردا نخوریم
title_in_english: O friend come let us not grieve for tomorrow

poem_in_farsi:
دوران جهان بی می و ساقی هیچ است،
بی زمزمهٔ نای عراقی هیچ است؛
هر چند در احوالِ جهان می‌نگرم،
حاصل همه عیش است و باقی هیچ است.
poem_in_english:
Dowrān-e jahān bi mey o sāqi hich ast,
Bi zamzame-ye nāy-e erāqi hich ast;
Har chand dar ahvāl-e jahān mi-negaram,
Hāsel hame eysh ast o bāqi hich ast.
poem_in_english_translation:
The world's course without wine and cupbearer is nothing,
Without the melody of the Iraqi flute is nothing;
The more I observe the state of the world,
The sum of it all is pleasure, and the rest is nothing.
meaning: Without joy and beauty, the world is meaningless. All that matters is the experience of living fully.
implications_for_21st_century: Strip away what doesn't bring joy. The essence of a good life is pleasure in its truest form.
poetic_traslation:
The course of time sans wine and love is naught,
Without a song, the sweetest air is naught;
However much I ponder worldly ways,
All ends in joy — the rest amounts to naught.
title_in_farsi: دوران جهان بی می و ساقی هیچ است
title_in_english: The world without wine and cupbearer is nothing

poem_in_farsi:
یک چند به کودکی به استاد شدیم،
یک چند ز استادی خود شاد شدیم؛
پایانِ سخن شنو که ما را چه رسید:
از خاک برآمدیم و بر باد شدیم.
poem_in_english:
Yek chand be kūdaki be ostād shodim,
Yek chand ze ostādi-ye khod shād shodim;
Pāyān-e sokhan shenow ke mā rā che rasid:
Az khāk bar-āmadim o bar bād shodim.
poem_in_english_translation:
For a while in childhood we sought a master,
For a while we were proud of our own mastery;
Hear the end of the tale — what became of us:
We came from dust and vanished into wind.
meaning: Life's journey from student to master ends the same for all — we return to nothingness.
implications_for_21st_century: No matter how much we learn or achieve, we all share the same fate. Humility is wisdom.
poetic_traslation:
A while in childhood at the master's feet,
A while in mastery, in triumph sweet;
Now hear the end of all that came to pass:
From dust we rose, and scattered in the heat.
title_in_farsi: یک چند به کودکی به استاد شدیم
title_in_english: For a while in childhood we sought a master
